summary: Lawrence E. Sullivan is a religious studies scholar who served as Professor of the History of Religions at Harvard Divinity School, Director of the Center for the Study of World Religions, and Professor of Theology at the University of Notre Dame.
Lawrence Heyworth Mills (1837–1918) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at New York University and later served as a professor at the University of Oxford.
Lawrence J. McCrea is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Sheldon Pollock. He serves as a professor at Cornell University.

Lawrence William Nelson is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Doctor of Philosophy and Religion from the California Institute of Integral Studies, alongside studies at institutions including Butler, Indiana, New York, and Northwestern universities, and St. John's College.
LeRoy Carr Barret (1877–1960) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Washington and Lee University and at Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield.
Leah Zahler was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, Harvey B. Aronson, and Geshe Wangyal.
Lee Yearley is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He served as a professor at Stanford University, where he is now Emeritus.

Leedom Lefferts is a scholar of Buddhist studies and anthropology. He served as Professor of Anthropology, Emeritus at Drew University and as a Research Associate in anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution.

Leela Aditi Wood is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College.

Leo Frobenius (1873–1938) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He held posts at the Frobenius Institute, Goethe University Frankfurt, Museum der Weltkulturen, and the Berlin Society for Anthropology, Ethnology, and Prehistory.

Leo M. Pruden (1938–1991) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Taitetsu Unno and Akira Hirakawa at the University of Tokyo, holding posts at Brown University, Nyingma Institute, and University of Oriental Studies.

Leo Meyer (1830–1910) was a linguist who studied under Theodor Benfey, Jacob Grimm, and Franz Bopp. He served as professor at the University of Göttingen and held a linguistics chair at the University of Tartu.
Leo Rishi Nelson Jones is an Indology and linguistics researcher who studied at and is a research project staff member at the University of Hamburg.

Leo Strauss (1899–1973) was a philosopher who studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, and Marburg universities. His career included academic posts at Cambridge, The New School, the University of Chicago, St. John's College, and Hebrew University.

Leon Hurvitz (1923–1992) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He served as a professor at the University of Washington from 1956 to 1971 and at the University of British Columbia from 1971 to 1988.

Leonard Bloomfield (1887–1949) was a linguist who studied at Harvard, Wisconsin, Chicago, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held professorships at Illinois, Ohio State, and Chicago, before serving as Sterling Professor of Linguistics at Yale.
Leonard Blussé (born 1946) is a historian and Sinologist. He studied at Leiden University and later served on its faculty from 1998 to 2011.
Leonard C. D. C. Priestley is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under A. K. Warder and held a post at the University of Toronto.

Leonard Swidler (1929–2026) was a religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Marquette, Wisconsin, and Tübingen. He served as Professor of Catholic Thought and Interreligious Dialogue at Temple University from 1966 to 2022.

id: P:Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp
summary: Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp (born 1952) is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned doctorates at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He taught at the University of Washington and chaired Sanskrit and Indian Studies at Harvard.
